description: Radxa ROCK 5C (Rockchip RK3588S2) dev board, on order. A board record: Atlas flashes it from maskrom (rockusb) with Rockchip's loader file and no vendor tool; running, it serves the identity contract (board-lite, gaia/device.toml), read-only. Written from rkdeveloptool, U-Boot and Radxa's docs; untested on this board.

storage_target_evidence: docs.radxa.com ROCK 5C introduction: one eMMC module connector (no module fitted by default) and a microSD slot; no SPI flash.
The image is a whole disk as Gaia writes it for eMMC (idblock at sector 64, U-Boot, partitions), written from byte 0.
instructions: Power the ROCK 5C off and take out any microSD card; fit the eMMC module.
Short the Maskrom pin hole with a DuPont wire (the ROCK 5C has no Maskrom button).
Connect the top USB 3.0 port (the OTG port) to this computer, then power the board on and remove the wire.
The board appears as 2207:350b (RK3588 maskrom). Atlas runs the loader's DDR init and usbplug, writes the image to the eMMC, reads it back and restarts the board.
todo: 2207:350b as RK3588 maskrom comes from secondary sources (MNT, Radxa's guides via search): rkdeveloptool 304f073's 99-rk-rockusb.rules stops at 350a and doesn't name it. Confirm with lsusb on the board.

The rkbin parts are in fetch.lock (not in git): rkbin f43a462's RK3588MINIALL.ini names rk3588_ddr_lp4_2112MHz_lp5_2400MHz_v1.18, rk3588_usbplug_v1.11 and rk3588_spl_v1.13, and builds rk3588_spl_loader_v1.18.113.bin with boot_merger. rkbin doesn't publish the merged file; Gaia's build (which runs boot_merger) is its source.

Whether the RK3588S2 takes the RK3588 loader unchanged. Gaia's ROCK 5C build ships rk3588_spl_loader_v1.18.113.bin (rkbin at its Buildroot 2026.02.3 pin, f43a462) next to sdcard.img; Atlas's parser reads it (chip 3588, 2 DDR entries incl. UsbHead, usbplug, FlashHead/Data/Boot, RC4 off) and its idblock agrees with its RKNS FlashHead, so only the board's run is left.
The cable: Radxa's guides differ between USB-A to USB-A and USB-A to USB-C for this port.
